uncited: All children of Standard Ray Casting share the following mechanism, terms, and mathematical formulation.
For each pixel, a ray $r(t) = O + tD$ is generated, where $O$ is the origin (camera position) and $D$ is the normalized direction.
If $t_{start} > t_{end}$, the ray misses the volume.
If the camera is inside the volume, $t_{start}$ is clamped to $0.0$ to prevent backward sampling [S5, S2350, unofficial].
At each step $i$, the sample position is $P_i = O + (t_{start} + i \cdot \Delta s)D$.
The scalar value $v$ at $P_i$ is obtained via trilinear interpolation from the 8 neighboring voxels of the 3D texture or grid [S4, S5, S7, S9, S23, S3161, S2350, unofficial].
